title: Register submit -> lock -> admin-reopen-with-reason -> resubmit
IMPORTANT_FLAG: This directly contradicts an architecture decision made earlier this session -- see notes below. Read this file before building anything else attendance-related.

mockup_description.layout: Two related screens: a locked 'Registre soumis' view, and a 'Registre rouvert' correction view.
key_elements: 'Registre soumis' screen: 'Soumis' + 'Verrouillé' status badges, class/subject/time/room/student-count header
Full student list with each one's FINAL locked status (label: 'Statut final')
'Voir les N autres élèves' progressive disclosure
Submission metadata: submitted-at timestamp, submitted-by (teacher name+role), register reference ID with copy button
'Modification désactivée' notice: 'Ce registre a été soumis et verrouillé. La modification directe n'est plus possible afin de garantir l'intégrité des données.'
'Demander une réouverture' (request reopen) button + 'Voir l'historique' link

'Registre rouvert' screen (after an admin grants the reopen): banner 'Réouvert par l'administration -- Cette séance a été rouverte pour correction', with a MANDATORY 'Motif' shown read-only (why it was reopened)
Per-student rows show a before/after diff when changed: 'Ancien statut -> Nouveau statut' (e.g. Absent -> Excusé), highlighted green, vs unchanged rows shown plainly
'Note de correction (obligatoire)' textarea the teacher must fill before resubmitting
Warning: 'Toutes les modifications seront journalisées et visibles dans l'historique du registre'
interactions: Submitting attendance creates an immutable, referenced 'register' -- not just a set of loose per-student rows
Once submitted, the register is LOCKED -- a teacher cannot silently edit past attendance

Correcting a locked register requires an admin-granted reopen with a stated reason, and the teacher must state a correction note before resubmitting -- a real two-party audit trail, not just an app-level toast

what_matches: The real attendance table's write pattern (delete existing row for that student/date/period, then reinsert) achieves idempotent correction today -- a teacher CAN correct a mistake, just not with any lock/reopen ceremony or audit trail around it

recordAudit() is called on every attendance mutation, so a raw event log of who-changed-what-when does technically exist in the generic auditLogs table -- just not surfaced as a register-centric view anywhere
what_differs: THERE IS NO REGISTER ENTITY AT ALL. Any teacher (or anyone with write access to that endpoint) can silently re-edit any past date's attendance at any time via POST /api/attendance, with zero lock, zero reopen request, zero mandatory reason, zero before/after diff shown to anyone.

This is not an oversight -- it was a deliberate architecture decision made in ATTENDANCE-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md (Section 1, this session): the attendanceRegisters / attendanceEntries / attendanceAuditEvents tables were found to have ZERO writers anywhere in the actual codebase at the time, and were DELETED as 'dead weight', with the explicit reasoning: 'if register-level locking ... turns out to be genuinely wanted later, it's a clean, small addition on top of the real attendance table then -- not lost by dropping the currently-empty tables now.'

These mockups are the evidence that register-level locking WAS genuinely wanted -- it's a first-class part of the product's mental model (two full mockup screens dedicated to it, plus register references appear again in the submission-confirmation and audit-log mockups). The earlier decision wasn't wrong given the information available at the time (those tables really were unused), but it should be revisited now that intent is clearer.

missing_to_add.item: DECISION NEEDED before building: rebuild a register concept (new table or a status column set added to a per-date/class/period grouping), OR achieve the same lock/reopen guarantee by adding a lightweight status + lockedAt/reopenedAt/reopenReason set of columns directly on top of the existing attendance rows (e.g. a small attendanceRegisters table with just id/tenantId/classSectionId/date/period/status/submittedAt/submittedById/lockedAt/reopenedAt/reopenedById/reopenReason, with attendance.registerId as a nullable pointer) rather than reviving the old entries/audit-event split
missing_to_add.notes: This is the single largest piece of missing scope revealed by the mockups. Recommend the lighter second option -- a status wrapper around the existing real attendance rows -- over reviving the old 3-table model, since the old model's per-entry duplication (attendanceEntries mirroring attendance) was itself part of why it was flagged as redundant.

missing_to_add.item: POST /api/attendance should refuse writes against a LOCKED register (reject with a clear error) unless a reopen has been granted
missing_to_add.notes: Currently there is no such guard at all -- any allowed role can silently overwrite locked history.

missing_to_add.item: 'Demander une réouverture' + admin-side approve/reject-reopen flow, mandatory reason on both the request and the grant
Before/after diff view when a reopened register is resubmitted
Register reference ID generation (e.g. REG-{date}-{classSectionCode}-{sequence}), surfaced in the submission-confirmation screen and the audit journal
